extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (schools, colleges, universities), school administrators, Title IX coordinators, lawyers and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how §106.31(a)(2) of the Title IX regulations applies to sex-separated treatment and duties to avoid causing more than de minimis harm, including scope, exceptions, standards for assessing harm, treatment of gender identity, athletics, facilities, documentation, and enforcement obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective harm standard (more than de minimis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harm under §106.31(a)(2) must be genuine and objectively non-trivial and assessed from the perspective of a reasonable person in the individual's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objective standard is grounded in longstanding anti-discrimination law and its injury requirement (e.g., Burlington N. & Santa Fe Ry. Co.). It avoids reliance on unusual subjective feelings; more-than-de-minimis harm is the trigger for a Title IX violation when otherwise-permissible sex separation or different treatment prevents participation consistent with gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: applies to separation/different treatment, not hostile environment standard
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.31(a)(2) applies to the manner in which a recipient carries out otherwise permissible different treatment or separation on the basis of sex; it does not apply to sex-based harassment (hostile environment) which is assessed under the sex-based harassment/hostile environment standard (§106.2) and the recipient's obligations under §106.44(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hostile environment addresses whether harassing conduct rises to discrimination; §106.31(a)(2) is distinct and focuses on separation/differentiation practices and whether those practices cause more than de minimis harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is covered (persons scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.31(a)(2) applies to any 'person', including students, employees, applicants for admission or employment, parents of minor students, students from other institutions, visiting lecturers, and other community members participating in a recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explicitly clarifies coverage beyond students to other participants or prospective participants in education programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory exceptions where more-than-de-minimis harm may be permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition on preventing a person from participating consistent with their gender identity does not apply when otherwise permitted by specific statutory/regulatory exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those exceptions are 20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(1)–(9) and the corresponding regulations at §§106.12–106.15; 20 U.S.C. 1686 and its regulation §106.32(b)(1) (sex-separate housing); and §106.41(b) (sex-separate athletic teams). Even where exceptions exist, recipients may voluntarily provide greater protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Athletics exception and program-wide equal opportunity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.31(a)(2) does not apply to male and female athletic teams a recipient offers under §106.41(b); longstanding athletics regulations permit individual exclusions that may impose more-than-de-minimis harm so long as program-wide equal athletic opportunity is provided under §106.41(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Athletics are evaluated at the program-wide level (equal opportunity for both sexes across the athletic program), not at the individual-team level. The Department is separately considering (via an Athletics NPRM) a standard for sport-related eligibility criteria where targeted, sport-related criteria may be permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to facilities, classes, appearance codes, and other sex-differentiated practices
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.31(a)(2) applies, with limited exceptions, to circumstances where recipients engage in permissible sex separation or differentiation including restrooms and locker rooms (§106.33), access to classes and activities (§106.34(a)-(b)), and policies such as appearance codes (dress and grooming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contexts without a statutory exception (e.g., restrooms, locker rooms, single-sex classes), preventing participation consistent with gender identity that causes more-than-de-minimis harm violates Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing access consistent with gender identity
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide access to sex-separate facilities and activities in a manner that does not cause more-than-de-minimis harm and must not prevent a person from participating consistent with their gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to bathrooms, locker rooms, classes, and similar contexts unless a statutory exception applies. Recipients retain discretion to provide sex-separated facilities consistent with nondiscrimination obligations but cannot justify more-than-de-minimis harm by pointing only to generalized physical differences between sexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining a person's gender identity (permissible evidence and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may rely on a student's consistent assertion of gender identity or written confirmation by the student or a parent, counselor, coach, or teacher to determine gender identity for purposes of §106.31(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not require invasive medical inquiries or burdensome documentation (e.g., amended birth certificate or evidence of medical treatment) to validate gender identity if such documentation is inaccessible or prohibited by law in that jurisdiction, because imposing such requirements imposes more-than-de-minimis harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonbinary students and individualized coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.31(a)(2) does not prescribe a single approach for nonbinary students; a recipient may coordinate with the student (and parent or guardian as appropriate) to determine how best to provide safe and nondiscriminatory access to facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include individualized arrangements developed with the student; recipients may provide but are not required to adopt a single uniform accommodation. Single-occupancy or gender-neutral facilities are acceptable options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on documentation requirements that cause harm
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not require a person to provide documentation (such as an amended birth certificate or evidence of medical treatment) to validate their gender identity for purposes of compliance with §106.31(a)(2) if access to such documentation is prohibited by law or if requiring it would impose more-than-de-minimis harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring invasive medical inquiries or burdensome documentation is itself a harm and thus inconsistent with §106.31(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation options and stigma considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer single-occupancy or gender-neutral facilities and other accommodations (including private alternatives) to students who seek additional privacy, but requiring transgender students to use separate facilities can be stigmatizing and harmful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering voluntary private options is permissible; however, policies that exclude students from participating consistent with their gender identity or that force segregated alternatives that stigmatize may violate §106.31(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment and other constitutional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.31(a)(2) does not override recipients' obligations to respect First Amendment, Due Process, and other constitutional rights; nothing in the regulations requires restricting speech or other rights protected against government action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not invoke Title IX to restrict speech in violation of the First Amendment. The Department will enforce Title IX consistent with constitutional guarantees; see §106.6(d) and the discussion of Hostile Environment Sex-Based Harassment—First Amendment Considerations (§106.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement obligation for sex-based harassment and harms in facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(a), a recipient must respond promptly and effectively when it knows of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment occurring in sex-separate facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients' obligations to address hostile environment harassment remain distinct from duties under §106.31(a)(2) but apply in parallel when discrimination or harassment arises in facilities or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on using generalized physiological differences to justify harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on generalizations about 'enduring physical differences' between men and women alone cannot substantiate categorical exclusions or justify causing more-than-de-minimis harm to a protected individual under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While Title IX permits some sex-based distinctions in contexts where separation is generally not harmful, such distinctions cannot be used to justify individual-level harms that exceed the de minimis threshold unless a statutory exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Athletics eligibility criteria (future standard under consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department signaled in an Athletics NPRM that a categorical ban on transgender students playing consistent with their gender identity would not satisfy a proposed standard, but more targeted criteria substantially related to sport, level of competition, and grade or education level could be permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is continuing to evaluate comments and will issue a final rule on criteria for a student's eligibility to participate on sex-separate athletic teams; until then, current athletics regulations (§106.41) continue to apply.
